conclusions.rationale: Exact final text/trailing-space normalization, all insertion outcomes and dispatch/publication errors are explicit. Reliable settlement transfers restoration ownership and starts the full duration from the eager write, rather than from initial publication; Steps 2/3/7 include the output/timing matrix. Clipboard publication failure is reported honestly, not counted as successful recovery.

source_citations.excerpt: every dictation that produces a non-empty final text places that text on the clipboard as plain text at the end of the insertion step, whatever the insertion method and whether insertion succeeded, failed or was skipped.

plan_citations.excerpt: After the existing insertion attempt settles (including key-injection failure), publish an eager plain-text recovery write and record its token/time.
Direct typing and ExternalScript use the same finally/handoff on success or failure; None and unavailable/skipped destination still reach it.
Timer uses deadline = continuous monotonic write time + captured duration.

conclusions.rationale: Ordered items/native representations are captured into owned data before the first write; empty is distinct from failed capture. Platform adapters, full-fidelity tests and explicit all-or-nothing fallback cover the behavior. macOS ownership-preserving replacement/clear remains a real Step 1 prerequisite/release blocker, not certified by this plan.

source_citations.excerpt: Before Handy first writes the clipboard for a dictation, it saves every representation of the previous clipboard content that the platform exposes

plan_citations.excerpt: Capture before the first Handy clipboard write of a non-cancelled non-empty output, including reliable promise publication.

Any inaccessible advertised representation, unsupported handle, incomplete enumeration, size overflow or unstable capture fails the **entire** recovery snapshot; never silently drop formats and call it full fidelity.
A failed fresh capture opens no recovery window and invokes the specified existing insertion behavior; no partial snapshot or long timer survives.
If public APIs cannot satisfy AC-003 race safety, block affected native implementation and request a scoped spec decision rather than inventing atomicity.

conclusions.rationale: Both ownership-token and exact-text fallback guards are planned at the actual final mutation boundary, with native two-process interference plus deterministic barriers. Same-text Linux re-copy limitation is explicitly retained from the source fallback; unresolved macOS TOCTOU blocks affected delivery rather than silently weakening the guarantee.

source_citations.excerpt: If the change counter differs at the end of the window (any copy by the user or another application), Handy leaves the clipboard untouched.

plan_citations.excerpt: Step 1 must establish an ownership-preserving restore primitive for multi-item replacement/clear, not just checkCount then clearContents.
Restore under the same OpenClipboard critical section after rechecking sequence
Restore only if exact UTF-8 transcript comparison succeeds; include current selection-owner token where exposed
Invariant guards cover a copy inserted immediately before native mutation; manual demonstrations of copy at 3 s alone cannot prove race safety.

conclusions.rationale: The corrected single serialized capture/publication/cancellation boundary and rollback checkpoint preserve the prior transcript, original snapshot and original deadline. After publication the guard uses the new transaction token, republishes the prior transcript only while still owned and unexpired, and rebinds ownership without restarting time. Already-expired checkpoints restore once; external copies cause no mutation and prior normal expiry skips. Pending providers/Enter/settlement are invalidated before rollback or ExplicitCopy. Consecutive output transfer, changed-copy recapture and orderly exit remain covered. Added Gherkin and Rollback state transitions plus barrier schedules resolve the initial cancellation ambiguity without weakening AC-004 or granting native feasibility in advance.

source_citations.excerpt: Cancelling a dictation does not open a window and leaves an already open window running unchanged.

plan_citations.excerpt: Cancellation and the first native mutation have one serialized linearization point.
Test ownership against the **new transaction's latest token**, never the superseded old token.
guardedly republish the checkpoint transcript, rebind its ownership token and resume its original generation with its original snapshot/deadline; do not create a new window or extend time.
If an external copy replaced the new transaction, perform no clipboard mutation; retain the checkpoint's original deadline until its normal ownership-check expiry, which skips restoration.
Rollback --> Open: guarded republish checkpoint, original deadline
Steps 2–4 tests must inject cancellation before/after first write, receipt, settle and old expiry, with/without external copy, and Copy during pending reliable settlement.

conclusions.rationale: History is outside the recovery module and tests assert existing count/content across every lifecycle event. WAV-gated history creation is qualified, not fabricated. Permanent CopyToClipboard bypasses recovery and closes old restoration ownership before its permanent output.

source_citations.excerpt: The window never deletes or modifies history entries.

plan_citations.excerpt: HistoryManager is not injected into restoration logic.
Switching to permanent mode on the next output closes old recovery without restoration before leaving the new transcript permanent.
SC-003 tests preexisting count **and contents**; native checks seed a successfully saved WAV entry before dictation/expiry/quit/crash proof.

conclusions.rationale: Shared descriptors and typed UI mutations enforce inclusive integer bounds and persisted defaults; immutable per-output capture defers changed policy to the next transcript. Deferred common Penflow work is authorized by the source and explicitly gates UI code; this review does not certify that missing design input.

suppress legacy restore only for eligible successful capture, preserve disabled/permanent behavior.

conclusions.rationale: Four FR-002 subtasks cover native owned snapshots, guarded coordinator decisions, pre-write capture and race/fidelity proof.
